input.quote: iii. Licensor hereby, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement, grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use covenant restricting the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, so the preferred position is met and no redline is warranted. Article II's restrictions (p0030, p0035, p0040-p0047) and the "Field of Use" definition (p0007) are limitations on the scope of the licence in the Licensed Technology itself — use confined to Spot FX market data and order entry, no sublicensing, no Derivative Works of the Licensed Technology — which are ordinary IP-scope limits on the licensed software, not restrictions on our own business activities; they leave us free to license, buy or build competing FX platforms. Article XI restrictions on distributing "the licensed programs" (p0027) and Article VI (p0085) are likewise product-specific and do not bind our business generally. Restrictions running the other way (the licence is non-exclusive to us) are not an issue for us. Noted but not flagged here: the Change of Control clause (p0134) lets Licensor deem consent reasonably withheld where an acquirer "conducts a business that is directly or indirectly competitive" with Licensor, and Article XXII (p0139) gives Licensor a right of first refusal over a sale of Licensee. Those constrain our M&A rather than our trading or product strategy and belong to the assignment/change-of-control rule, so we do not double-count them as a non-compete. The three-year post-term non-solicitation of Licensor employees (p0125) is a personnel covenant, not a non-compete, and falls outside this rule.
